title: OSHA Lockout Tagout Checklist (29 CFR 1910.147)
subtitle: For supervisors checking an energy control procedure, a lockout in progress or LOTO records on site.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A, and record the machine, date and inspector at the top.
For each Defect, note what was found, who will correct it and by when; do not start servicing until isolation items are corrected.
The machine manufacturer's instructions and your site's rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Program and written procedures
items: A documented energy control procedure exists for the machine, or all eight conditions of the documentation exception apply
Procedure lists machine-specific steps for shutting down, isolating, blocking and securing
Procedure states how devices are placed, removed and transferred and who is responsible
Procedure states how to test the machine to verify that energy controls work
Lockable isolation on new or modified equipment
Isolating devices on machines installed, replaced or majorly repaired or modified after January 2, 1990 accept a lock
Where tags are used on lockable devices, they sit where the lock would go and the equivalent-safety demonstration is on file

sections.title: Locks, tags and hardware
items: Locks, tags, chains, wedges, key blocks, adapter pins or self-locking fasteners are available to workers from the employer
LOTO locks and tags are singularly identified and not used for toolboxes, lockers or other purposes
Devices match by color, shape or size; tags share one print and format
Tags are intact and legible in wet, damp or corrosive locations
Self-locking, non-reusable attachment of at least 50 pounds unlocking strength, equivalent to a one-piece nylon cable tie
Every lock and tag shows the name or identity of the employee who applied it
Tags carry a warning such as Do Not Start or Do Not Operate

sections.title: Applying lockout or tagout
items: Locks and tags were applied by the authorized employees doing the work
Affected employees were told before controls were applied
A lock or tag is on each energy isolating device feeding the machine
Each lock physically holds its isolating device in the safe or off position
Residual pressure, springs, raised parts and similar stored energy are relieved, restrained or blocked
The authorized employee confirmed deenergization before starting work
Every crew member has a personal lock or tag on the group device or lockbox
On-site and outside employers have exchanged their lockout or tagout procedures
A written method transfers lock or tag protection from off-going to oncoming workers

sections.title: Release from lockout or tagout
items: Nonessential items removed and machine components operationally intact before release
All employees safely positioned or out of the area before re-energizing
Affected employees told devices are off before the machine is started
Each device removed by the employee who applied it, or under the documented absent-employee procedure

sections.title: Periodic inspection and training records
items: Inspection of this procedure dated within the last year
Inspector is an authorized employee who does not use the procedure being inspected
Record names the machine, date, employees included and the person who inspected
Authorized employees can name the energy sources, their type and magnitude and the isolation method for this machine
Where tagout is used, training covers the tag limitations listed in the standard
Training record shows each employee's name and training dates and is current

references: 29 CFR 1910.147: The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
Source: eCFR, Title 29, Part 1910 Subpart J (text as of 2026-11-09)
